items.name: DeepSeek Harness Desktop v0.2
items.summary: DeepSeek shipped v0.2 of its open-source Harness agent runtime as ready-to-run desktop installers for macOS (Apple silicon) and 64-bit Windows, adding in-app plugin installation/management, scheduled automation tasks, and an experimental mode where the agent writes plugins from conversation. The MIT-licensed repo sits near 242k GitHub stars, marking open-source agentic tooling crossing from developer tool to consumer product.

items.name: Ivo Sage
items.summary: Ivo released Sage, the first free open-source model from a legal AI company, built by post-training DeepSeek V4 Flash on long-horizon contract work with public and synthetic data from real attorneys. After RL it jumped from 70% to 91% on the LAB Contracts benchmark, matching much larger frontier models at a fraction of the cost.

items.name: Cantina Apex Flash-1
items.summary: Cantina Security released apex-flash-1, open-weights model post-trained from GLM-5.3-Flash with GRPO on 150 tasks generated from 50 of the company's real vulnerability cases, plus an 'abliterated' low-refusal variant for researchers. It solves 40/60 held-out security tasks at $2.38 total vs $74.68 for Claude Opus 5 High — a bet that defenders need locally runnable, cheap security-worker models.

items.name: Talus Bio Ptarmigan-1
items.summary: Talus Bio released Ptarmigan-1 via a public portal, the first AI model to predict small-molecule binding sites across the whole human proteome without 3D structures — opening the ~40% of proteins, including disordered and historically undruggable targets, that structure-based methods can't touch. It outperformed structure-based methods on a STAT6 inhibitor series and screens 3.4B compounds in a day.

items.name: ELYZA-Thinking-1.0 (32B/33B)
items.summary: Japan's ELYZA released two open Apache-2.0 reasoning models based on NII's domestic llm-jp-4 series — a 33B dense and a 32B-A3B MoE — trained for complex instruction following, math, coding and Japanese-specific knowledge retrieval, alongside its new RSI research group for recursive self-improvement. In one customer-service experiment, a self-improving agent raised task completion from 34.3% to 52.9% while cutting inference cost 67%.
